tws-soundcore-liberty-4.review: Ordinary sound. V-shaped. Good driver; such a shame about the tuning, sharp at the top. Even with EQ cut all the way down it's still quite bright. Maybe different tips would help. If you're just after the sound, the Liberty 3 Pro is enough, unless you want better eartips and fit than the L3 Pro; then try this. Mic is OK.

tws-1more-comfobuds-pro.review: The ANC is interesting: Strong, Mild and pass-through, so you can hear your surroundings while listening. The Strong ANC is nice too. You can assign gestures freely: what tap-and-hold, double tap and triple tap do.

tws-airpods-pro-2.review: Terrible value at this price if you actually use it for music: plenty are better. If you want a good mic, plenty of those are good too, or buy a USB mic and still have change. No aptX, no LDAC, weak battery. "But the ecosystem auto-connects!" Every flagship auto-connects now; it doesn't matter. Preset EQ only at this price? FUCKING HELL. At 500k rupiah maybe OK, but then there's the Dot 3i. Only the ANC is good; it can rival the Sony XM4.

tws-sony-c700.review: Warm, more or less the same as the C500. ANC is good and natural, no submerged feeling, but sadly not LinkBuds S level: natural enough but not as quiet. Safe, warm sound. AAC codec, unlike other 1-million-rupiah TWS that already have aptX/LDAC, though the AAC isn't bad. Lots of rivals like Edifier or the Soundcore L4NC beat it on value. On durability, Sony is probably safe. Tonality is fine: warm and bassy, EQable. Soundstage and separation struggle against the EarFun FP3. But the ANC and mic are still among the best at the price. (TWS battle review on his YouTube.)

tws-huawei-freebuds-se-4-anc.review: Great driver, far from the overhyped Baseus BP1 Pro. Good ANC, decent. Custom EQ. The default tonality is a bit too bassy and airy (typical Huawei U-shape), but the driver and the sense of room are good. For 299k it's almost too good. Its tonality beats Tozo's in my view: tidier, grander. Soundstage and imaging aren't at the EarFun Air Pro 4i's level yet. Killer, a no-brainer. STOP FUCKING BUYING 100k TWS. SAVE UP FOR THIS. 200–300k is the new benchmark. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-soundcore-r60i-nc.review: The driver and bass are much better than the R50i NC. An improvement. But Soundcore's EQ still bottoms out at 100 Hz, so even if you lower it, 80, 60 and 30 Hz stay higher than on the Huawei SE4. If you ask me, sound-wise the SE4 is easier to balance than this. But casual listeners will like it, and it's no longer as murky as the R50i NC. Annoyingly, the Huawei SE4 has NO MULTIPOINT (look it up: it can't connect to two devices at once). ANC is tidier with less white noise than the SE4. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-roseselsa-ceramic-mkii.review: Driver is OK. Sadly no custom EQ, but the HiFi preset is the best of them: not too bassy, and the mids aren't too recessed. The tonal weakness is that the upper mids are too high for me, and 8 kHz is still pointy, though not as much as the upper mids. Weak mic, ordinary ANC, small eartips.

tws-sony-wf-c510.review: More punch than the C500; a different driver, nice tonality. But soundstage and imaging aren't as wide as the Air Pro 4. A really proper mic: not much noise reduction, but loud, it even cuts through a hijab. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-jbl-wave-beam.review: It's OK: a decent JBL, not overpriced, but not cheap-feeling either. Balanced. The mids and highs spread out to the left and right, slightly forward, while the low end sits in the middle behind your head, which makes for nice imaging. Again, when a big brand makes a cheap product something gets nerfed, and here it's ANC: there's none, just transparency. That's it. The rest, sound quality etc., is very safe. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-jabra-elite-10.review: The bass is very tidy, with bass-rumble technicalities that can compete with the Sony XM5 class. Downsides: still only AAC, a price I still find expensive, and patented eartips and nozzle that will be hard to replace one day. ANC is very quiet, focused on low-mids down to sub-bass; it still gives that pressure in the ears. So I think the value is still a stretch. The TWS isn't bad; at around 1–1.5 million rupiah it'd make more sense.

tws-jabra-elite-8-active.review: Still too overpriced; I suggest the Edifier NeoBuds Pro 2 or LinkBuds S. A bit bassy. Mic is OK. Rugged, dust- and water-resistant.

tws-oppo-enco-buds3s.review: On a discount down to around 200k it's actually still OK. For a fairly big brand like Oppo the driver isn't bad: clear and good, better than Tozo, less airy. Still lots of sub-bass, but the Pure Vocal preset is fine. There's a custom EQ, but it's half-baked: only 6 bands, and moving them doesn't change the gain much. Mic is OK. No ANC. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-tozo-aerosound-3.review: KING OF MIC at 200k. A clear driver, brighter than the Clear; the Clear's highs are smoother, warm, smooth and lush, while this one's more aggressive. The bass rumble is also wider and punchier, but not as murky and boomy as the R50i NC. Has ANC, light, about R50i NC class. EQ presets can be shared between users; I'll make one. Sound is in the same class as the Clear; it comes down to preference. I'm sure many budget buyers will prefer this, because the Clear feels more neutral and smooth while this is brighter and hits more fun. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-soundpeats-clear.review: 40-hour battery with a serious custom EQ: you can cut bass from 125 Hz down to 30 Hz and below, so it won't be as BOOMY as the Eggel or the Soundcore R50i and A20i. You can raise the volume further on the TWS even when the phone is at max. Gaming mode, app support. (Video review on his YouTube.)

tws-tozo-aersound-nc9.review: For people who like the bean shape and want ANC. The ANC competes well with QCY: it's good. Transparency still has a little white noise. The sound is fairly bright at 8–10 kHz, so it suits low-volume listening. I'm not a fan of the tonality, but the driver isn't murky; definitely OK. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-qcy-buds-anc.review: The quietest ANC compared with Tozo, SoundPeats and Soundcore. The driver isn't bad. Number one is still the Clear and Aersound, then this, then the R50i NC; the R50i NC is murkier and boomier. Here you can still reduce the bass; it's not as boomy as the R50i NC. The Clear and Aersound have better mics. Lots of noise-cancelling features and environment modes.

tws-redmi-buds-8-lite.review: Old-school V-shape: too much mid-bass, the mids cut a lot. The custom EQ let me fix it somewhat, but it's quite hard to reach JM-1. After EQ it sounds broadly like the R60i NC. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-redmi-buds-6-lite.review: I slightly prefer the Clear; its vocals are good. This one is still quite bassy, but the driver resolution isn't as murky as the R50i NC, so it's still very OK, and it has a custom EQ. Has ANC and transparency, still very light. The mic is very OK. Sounds better than the R50i NC, but the R50i NC has multipoint.

tws-earfun-air-life.review: Already good, with custom EQ control. For some reason the driver on the SoundPeats Clear sounds more open, brighter and clearer, but this isn't bad, and it's cheaper than the Clear: only 229k. Mic is not bad either. This is EarFun's first attempt to conquer the 200k budget, and it's not bad. (Video review on his YouTube.)

tws-lypertek-z7.review: King of battery, without sacrificing the sound: really good. Shame about the price; at around 2.2 million it might be more popular. A less-known name, but it sounds good. Sadly no ANC for those who need it, but it has transparency.

tws-baseus-bp1-ultra.review: Same story: the EQ still wrecks it, though the stock tonality isn't as bassy as the BP1 Pro. The treble is very rolled-off/warm. Not much of an improvement.

tws-baseus-bp1-pro.review: Driver isn't bad, and casual listeners will like the default tuning. But the custom EQ is a lie, like there's no custom EQ at all: it makes a mess of things. Mic is not bad. The ANC makes you dizzy. Not bad, but many reviews of it are misleading. (His full honest review is on YouTube.)

tws-soundpeats-c30.review: Just skip it. Murky, weird, muffled, hard to fix. Go for Oppo, Tozo, Huawei or Soundcore instead.

tws-soundcore-r50i-nc.review: More complete features than the regular R50i. The noise cancelling is real, not a gimmick, but still very light; I'd strongly recommend the Dot 3i. The sound is an improvement over the Dot 3i, but for technicalities and tuning I prefer the SoundPeats Clear. Mic is OK (4 AI mics), the battery is upgraded and the case doubles as a phone stand, which is unique. Get this if you don't need great sound, love lots of bass, and want to try ANC. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-lypertek-z5.review: A sound upgrade over the Z3: the low-mids and bass are more correct, not too boomy. Has ANC, and it's not bad. Sound is OK and it gets really loud. The battery isn't as big as the Z3's any more, though, since it now has ANC.

tws-earfun-air-pro-3.review: Bassy. The Free Pro 3 has better tonality and nicer staging. Here 8 kHz is quite forward, but it can be EQ'd. Sub-bass can be cut down to 60 Hz; Soundcore bottoms out at 100 Hz so its sub-bass can't be cut further, but this can. Nice. Good ANC. REALLY GOOD MIC. Gaming mode with 55 ms delay.

tws-soundpeats-capsule-3-pro.review: Shouty and sharp. It can be EQ'd (see his EQ table) to be better. The treble is a bit grainy and rough; it's a SoundPeats driver after all. But you can reduce the bass so it isn't too boomy or muddy. Battery lasts forever. LDAC. Mic is decent. 80 ms latency, better than the Air Pro 3. If you don't care too much about sound it's actually not bad at all, and fairly affordable.

tws-redmi-buds-4-pro.review: Neutral with a bass-boost tuning. The default tuning is already OK compared with the Dot 3i's default. Better mic too. Pleasant, good fit. For people who don't want anything fancy, it just works. Go for it.

tws-earfun-free-2s.review: LOW-LATENCY GAMING MODE. Has a custom EQ. Balanced, fun sound. If you feel the Dot 3i lags too much, this is the answer. Its only weakness is no ANC. The EQ goes down to 60 Hz, unlike the Dot 3i's 100 Hz, so you can really suppress sub-bass if you don't like a lot, or push it if you do.

tws-moondrop-golden-ages.review: Hard to place against other consumer TWS, and the price doesn't help. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-moondrop-space-travel.review: Main weakness: battery. The tuning is lovely. Technicalities are a little lacking in detail and soundstage, and treble extension is a bit short. The rest is fine. 55 ms game mode at a very low price. Sounds nice without custom EQ. Mic is ordinary. Also, the case has no lid. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-moondrop-ultrasonic.review: The tuning is fine, but no custom EQ yet, light ANC, overpriced. Only 18 hours of battery. Ordinary mic. Imaging and soundstage are too narrow. Just get the EarFun Air Pro 4. Low volume. It sounds about the same as the Space Travel; even if it's an improvement, it's not much. Other brands are far better, especially on features.

tws-soundcore-vr-p10.review: Ultra-low latency in dongle mode: the dongle plugs into the phone's USB-C (Android only), under 30 ms. For me even 50–60 ms isn't very noticeable; this is even less so. V-shaped sound, but it also offers a special gaming tuning. Connects to PS4, PS5, Switch, PC, laptop and phone, plug and play with the dongle.

tws-soundpeats-mini-pro.review: Skip to the Engine 4, Dot 3i or Air 2.

tws-audio-technica-sq1tw2.review: CLEAR MIC. No noise reduction, but it's really nice. A good brand whose TWS line really suffers; this is the newest, cheapest one. Overpriced. SBC codec. Tuning presets, but the default is very V-shaped: treble too bright, too much bass. Switch to the VOCAL preset and the mids are right but the treble gets brighter. The BASS preset is even more V-shaped. Tricky. No ANC, has transparency. What does it even want to be? I admit the style and mic are the best, and the driver itself really isn't bad. It just needs tuning.

tws-soundpeats-trueengine3-se.review: Sounds good. Has a custom EQ. Fairly bassy. Fit is a bit trickier than the Dot 3i. The mic is truly unusable, really bad compared with the Dot 3i.

tws-audio-technica-cks50tw.review: This is good, and the EQ is good: sensitive, even 1 dB is clearly audible. A properly great EQ. ANC is not Sony level. The sound has a lot of lower mids, bunched up; that's why I EQ it down so the vocal midrange is clearer and not muddy. And the EQ really works. The bass timbre is very OK too.

tws-redmi-buds-3-pro.review: The driver is good and fairly detailed; the midrange is very OK, not cheap-sounding, a 9 mm DD. Not boomy. Sounds better than the Honor Earbuds 2 Lite. The mic is really good too: better than Sony, comparable with the Edifier NeoBuds Pro.

tws-honor-earbuds-2-lite.review: The noise cancelling is good compared with the SoundPeats T3, though I find the awareness mode a bit lacking. Still bassy, but not as bloated or boomy as the Fantech Mithril TX1 Pro. The battery lasts 32 hours, great. A very low-budget AirPods replacement. Still, better to just get the Dot 3i.

tws-soundcore-x10.review: Most people will like this TWS. The ear hooks are comfortable and don't wobble when running. Has gaming mode, ANC, and a relaxation mode that helps pace your breathing. BIG, WIDE BASS.

tws-lypertek-z3-mark-2-0.review: 7 + 70 hours of battery, absolutely insane. The sound is also very OK, very good value and powerful. Good tuning, not shouty; people will surely love the bass, though the soundstage isn't very grand. The WATERPROOFING is crazy: you can drop it in a glass of water and it's fine. (He suggests trying a demo at CSI Zone, Pamulang.)

tws-moondrop-nekocake.review: Tuning OK, driver OK. Sadly the Bluetooth codec is still AAC/SBC; with aptX on the same driver the vocal and cymbal detail would be even better. Has ANC. The voice prompts when you switch ANC modes, connect etc. sound like an anime girl character. The driver and tuning sound so good, and punchy. Low volume. The app isn't great.

tws-edifier-x3-pro.review: Why is it still SBC? Come on Edifier, at least give us AAC, please. The custom EQ isn't a 10-band EQ yet either; it loses to Tozo and EarFun. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-vyatta-airboom-anc-s.review: The FIRST TWS with the FERNANDA GUNSAN SIGNATURE sound. By default it's muffled and very bassy, but there's now an EQ preset I made to fix that and balance it. The ANC is still a gimmick in my view, very light. Mic is OK and proper, battery OK, fit OK. A shame the driver and default sound could be better. Hoping local products keep improving.

tws-sony-wi-c100.review: A good neckband. Good mic. Balanced sound, better than Sony's wired in-ears under 300k rupiah; this is the better buy. Has custom EQ, play/pause/next/previous and volume controls, and Sony-style DSEE upscaling. Trust me, this is nicer than the XB400, which can't even be EQ'd in Sony's app.
